findings.evidence: `Representation.tensorSquareEquivSymmetricExterior` at `Tensor/Square.lean:44-50` assumes only `[CommRing R] [Invertible (2 : R)]`, while `stdRep`, `tensorPowerRep`, `symPowerRep`, `extPowerRep`, and `FDRep` are all defined over commutative rings.
findings.fix: Move these two declarations to a `[CommRing k] [Invertible (2 : k)]` section; retain a field-specific convenience wrapper only if needed.
findings.issue: `tensorSquareRepEquiv` and `tensorSquareFDRepIso` are restricted to fields, although the generic equivalence and all standard-representation APIs used here work over a commutative ring with invertible `2`.

findings.evidence: For eigenvalues/formal diagonal entries, `tr(Sym² g)+tr(⋀² g)=Σᵢ λᵢ²+2Σᵢ<ⱼ λᵢλⱼ=(tr g)²`, a polynomial identity valid in every characteristic; the current `NeZero` is introduced only at line 90 to invoke the splitting.
findings.fix: Prove the character identity independently of the splitting and remove `NeZero`; then place `char_tensorSquare_stdRep` in a plain `[Field k]` section as well.
findings.issue: `char_tensorSquare` unnecessarily assumes `[NeZero (2 : R)]`; the trace identity holds in characteristic two as well, even though the direct-sum splitting used by this proof does not.

summary: The standard-representation decomposition and character identity carry stronger scalar assumptions than their natural statements require.
